comment: Seaways narrower than the continental pass's 10 km lattice, which the pass burns into its node elevations where the terrain is today's (rivers Task 8b, round 2): each polyline's nodes are lowered to the sill depth, moved with the era's own shift from the present-day overview, so an era whose sea stood below the sill keeps the basin closed. Read by timefly_core::hydrology::straits and by Task 11's Python.

straits.name: Bosporus
straits.source: Bosporus Strait centreline from the Sea of Marmara to the Black Sea; sill about 35 m below present sea level (published bathymetry of the strait's saddle)
straits.note: The strait is 0.7-3.5 km wide and about 31 km long: below the 5' overview and the lattice, so without it the Black Sea is an inland basin that merges with the Caspian through the Manych.
